claim: Putting thousands of MCP tool schemas in one prompt eventually exceeds useful context and tool selection capacity.
The proposed pattern uses a small stable tool that obtains a relevant subset of tools for the task.
Candidate tools can be selected with simple deterministic rules or embedding retrieval.
Tool descriptions affect model selection and may need to be rewritten when tools are hard to distinguish.
Remote MCP tool descriptions can inject unsafe instructions if accepted without controls.
The demo defines action tools dynamically at runtime rather than compiling the whole set into the prompt.
The speakers note that embedding based narrowing still needs a deliberate retrieval design.
